youtube.title: The Ramayana Began With One Arrow… and a Sage's Tears 🏹 | Valmiki Story
youtube.description:
One arrow. One crying bird. One sage's grief, and the Ramayana was born. 🏹😢

Before Lord Rama's story was ever told, Maharishi Valmiki watched a hunter kill one of a pair of Krauncha birds on the banks of the Tamasa river. His sorrow (shoka) poured out as the first shloka, and that verse became the Ramayana, the Adi Kavya (first poem).

📜 The first shloka:
"Mā niṣāda pratiṣṭhāṁ tvam agamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ…" (Valmiki Ramayana 1.2.15)

🎨 RAMAYANA: The Epic in Chalk, Episode 1
Maharishi Valmiki's Ramayana, retold one chalk drawing at a time.

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda, sargas 1–2

instagram.caption:
The Ramayana began with a bird's death.

By the Tamasa river, a hunter's arrow struck a krauncha bird.
Maharishi Valmiki's grief came out as a verse, the first shloka:
"Ma nishada pratishtham tvam agamah shashvatih samah…"
Then Brahma asked him to tell Rama's whole story in that metre.
